{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZhe92g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDIeCo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 107, "title": "Add an evidence-qualified forum unread listing and next-unread reading journey", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `eaf30b4643ecf96dcf563301bb7cd12eb201952f`, forum users can list posts with unread/read markers and open `READ number`, but cannot list only unread posts or read the next unread contribution. A routine reading round requires repeatedly choosing numbers from the full list.

This is an existing fidelity gap, not a demonstrated regression from the Archie merge. It affects the core SIG experience and is the next priority identified by the latest assessment.

## Expected outcome

Provide this terminal journey in existing forum destinations:

`forum → UNREAD → NEXT → repeated NEXT → no-unread response → BACK`

- `UNREAD` lists existing posts whose numbers exceed the selected human's forum marker, in ascending number order, preserving their original numbers and reply references.
- `NEXT` opens the lowest existing number above that marker and persists the read through the existing `markRead` transaction before displaying its body.
- Every command uses fresh content and the current selected human. Missing numbers are skipped naturally.
- `LIST` remains the complete list. `UNREAD` need not introduce a persistent filtering mode or separate reader cursor; HELP retains normal forum guidance.

Accept these names and one-post-at-a-time behavior as **category D reconstruction**. They are not authenticated PC-VAN host commands or an emulation of client autopilot software.

## Context

### Historical evidence and tolerance

Sources researched live on 2026-10-24:

- The [まいとーく client-author description](https://www.vector.co.jp/soft/win95/net/se024554.html) explicitly lists unread retrieval/writing for forum-related services. Confidence is high in the listed capability; exact release dating and applicability throughout 1996 remain unresolved. Grouped client features do not establish identical service workflows or host syntax.
- The [ATPMAC author-description search excerpt](https://www.vector.co.jp/soft/dos/net/se015876.html) specifically describes visiting SIG forums to read unread contributions. Direct retrieval returned a cache miss. Treat this as supplementary snippet-only evidence, with unresolved dating.
- An [indexed PCVAN_DL.PRO 1.08 catalog entry](https://search.vector.co.jp/vsearch/vsearch.php?kanji=euc&key=PR&start=1160) dated August 15, 1996 describes automated forum retrieval/contribution. Direct retrieval failed. It supplies limited target-year context, not proof of particular unread commands or marker semantics.
- A fresh inspection of [Internet Magazine, April 1995, pp. 104–105](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199504-104-bbs.pdf) places Return-key unread reading in ASAHI Net coverage and group unread tracking in NIFTY-Serve coverage. Neither authenticates PC-VAN controls. Previously excluded fictional NEURON transcripts and modern schematic screens also remain unsuitable for command authentication.

Focused searches recovered no qualifying target-year PC-VAN unread-reader sequence. Inaccessible client/catalog pages did not stop investigation; the readable client-author page and contemporary publisher comparison supplied useful evidence and service-context boundaries.

**Accepted reconstruction:** reuse the existing per-human/per-forum high-water mark. Reading number N marks numbers through N read, even if the user did not open each body. This is an existing implementation tolerance, not established historical tracking behavior. Preserve it explicitly; do not silently introduce individual-post read tracking. Confidence is high in implementation feasibility and moderate in the experiential reconstruction. Command spelling, Japanese guidance and exact interaction sequence remain authored choices.

### Implementation and history

- `src/navigation.ts:handleForum` currently accepts LIST and numbered READ; `renderForum` derives markers from `lastReadNumber`.
- `src/main.ts` refreshes repository content before forum commands, but only recognizes numbered READ for read persistence. NEXT must resolve, persist and render the same contribution without independently selecting a different post after the marker changes.
- `src/forums.ts` supplies sorted posts, local/demo precedence, reply resolution and established identity/date/body rendering.
- `src/storage/repository.ts:markRead` validates the human and post and transactionally takes the maximum marker. Reuse it without schema or backup-format changes.
- [The storage contract](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/eaf30b4643ecf96dcf563301bb7cd12eb201952f/docs/local-storage.md#forum-reading) documents high-water semantics and next-command cross-tab refresh.

[Issue #8](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/8) established composition and read tracking; it did not require next-unread reading. [Issue #33](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/33) preserves genuinely empty local collections. Live open-Issue and open-PR queries returned no items; an exact next-unread history search returned no match. Duplicate detection remains terminology-dependent.

[PR #106](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/106) and `docs/validation.md` record 383 passing checks using three workers, including configured type checking/build. These are Coordinator records, not checks performed by this graph. Default/eight-worker reliability remains unresolved.

Scope is existing forums only. Keep host paging, batch retrieval, subscriptions, marker-reset controls, mail/conference/NetNews unread features, Wakaba and other service expansion separate.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement and advertise UNREAD and NEXT in MITI 資料室, DAISIZEN forums and the additional existing SIG boards. Preserve case/whitespace normalization, numbered READ, composition/replies, full LIST, HELP and actual BACK/MAIN parent paths. Reject malformed arguments without navigation or writes. Blank input must not silently read a post.
- [ ] Resolve unread candidates from fresh content and the current selected human before each command. Default an absent marker to zero; select by existing post number, independently of timestamps, storage order and gaps. Persist and render the same selected post through the established rendering path. Consecutive queued NEXT commands must advance rather than repeat a stale candidate; subsequent commands must observe other-tab content, selection and marker changes without moving markers backwards.
- [ ] UNREAD, LIST, HELP, invalid commands and exhausted NEXT leave read state unchanged. Successful NEXT updates only the selected human/forum marker through existing transactional semantics. Failed marker writes report a retryable error and display no newly selected body, matching the current numbered-READ safeguard. Refresh/storage failures and stale-world replacement must not continue using obsolete selections.
- [ ] With no selectable human, give concise HANDLE guidance while preserving anonymous LIST/READ browsing; do not force registration or create a marker. Distinguish no unread contributions from unavailable/ambiguous mappings using existing empty-state conventions. Empty, missing and restored-empty collections stay empty; browsing must not create boards, copy demos or seed records. Legacy demo-only controller behavior must not acquire persistent personal read state.
- [ ] Add focused tests using existing Playwright/controller/repository helpers. Include a gapped fixture such as numbers 1, 4 and 9 with marker 3: UNREAD lists 4/9, NEXT reads 4 then 9, and exhaustion writes nothing. Cover absent/exhausted markers, numbered READ high-water behavior, human/forum isolation, current-name/date/reply rendering, rapid queued commands, other-tab refresh, failed read writes and retry, reload/JSON round-trip, restore/reset and anonymous/empty/ambiguous cases. Exercise a production terminal journey through the connection wrapper and verify command ownership during composition and other services.
- [ ] Preserve functional, storage, consent, composition/IME and terminal regression coverage. Deterministic protected-record comparisons should allow only the intended read marker and normal session/activity/history updates; members, SIGs/forums/posts, mail and unrelated settings remain unchanged. Retain literal Japanese/markup rendering, input focus, simulated IME submission guards, terminal logs and pacing/skip behavior. No model download, real inference or new network service is needed.
- [ ] Update README, storage/research documentation and discoverable Settings/About provenance with actual controls, high-water consequences, source dates/access limitations and category D assumptions. Keep routine Japanese forum output concise. The Coordinator runs focused checks and the complete existing suite before merge, for example `npm test -- tests/forums.spec.ts tests/composition.spec.ts tests/journey.spec.ts tests/repository.spec.ts --workers=3` followed by `npm test -- --workers=3`; configured servers already perform type checking/build. Record actual results, failures and worker settings accurately. Review the final diff, affected links and `git diff --check`; preserve the unresolved default-worker limitation rather than claiming it resolved.

## Optional validation

Compare with a subsequently recovered dated PC-VAN manual/session. Native Japanese IME or former-user feedback may refine presentation, but neither is a mandatory completion gate.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks are achievable before merge against local production assets.

Evaluation baseline: `eaf30b4643ecf96dcf563301bb7cd12eb201952f`.
